createdBy: code review R8, agent A (2 sites) + implementer measurement (3rd site, reachability, T-004 note)
impact:
Python's `re` on `str` patterns makes `\d` match the whole Unicode **Nd** category; JavaScript's `\d` is ASCII `0-9` only. Three ported regexes in `src/codex.ts` inherit that narrowing. Measured (ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE, U+0663) — all three diverge, python matches, port does not:

| site | subject | python | port |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROLLOUT_RE` (codex.ts:32) | `rollout-2026-07-0<AR3>T00-43-18-019f45d4-…` | match | no match |
| `DATE_DIR_RE` (codex.ts:34) | `2026/07/0<AR3>` | match | no match |
| `SCRATCHPAD_RE` (codex.ts:40) | `/tmp/claude-<AR3><AR9>/x` | match | no match |

Agent A's round-8 review named the first two; `SCRATCHPAD_RE` is a **third site it did not report**, found by sweeping every `\d` in the file.

**These are success-path divergences, not error-message ones:**
- `ROLLOUT_RE` / `DATE_DIR_RE` gate date-windowing. A session Python windows and counts, the port instead pushes into the "could not be date-windowed and were excluded" bucket (usage.py:410) — different totals AND a different byte-frozen coverage line.
- `SCRATCHPAD_RE` decides whether a cwd collapses to the scratchpad label. Python collapses it; the port emits a full encoded-path project row instead — a different row in the table.

**Reachability differs per site.** Rollout filenames and date dirs are generated by codex itself with ASCII digits, so those two are effectively unreachable. `SCRATCHPAD_RE` matches a **user's real cwd** read out of the rollout log, so it is the one that is merely improbable rather than machine-impossible.

**The fix already exists in this repo.** `src/dates.ts:45` solved exactly this for `norm_date` and deliberately does NOT use JS's `\p{Nd}`: V8 ships a newer Unicode database than the reference CPython (measured: 760 Nd code points vs CPython 3.11.6's 660), so the native class would accept ~100 code points Python rejects. `src/unicode-tables.ts` holds the pinned table and `isDecimalDigit()` is the predicate. These three regexes should be rebuilt against that same table so all four sites share one definition of "digit".

**Also note for T-004 (not yet ported):** `usage.py:777` has `re.fullmatch(r"-\d+d", argv[i+1])` in the argument parser, and `int()` accepts Nd too — so `--since -<AR3>d` genuinely works in Python today (`int("<AR3>")` is 3). `normDate` in `src/dates.ts` already handles this correctly; the CLI's argument *detection* regex must not reintroduce ASCII-only `\d` when it is ported.

**Scope:** pre-existing (T-003 wrote these regexes). `git diff --stat` confirms T-006's changes to `src/codex.ts` are confined to the new `pyGet` helper and its two call sites — lines 32-40 are untouched — so this is filed rather than fixed inline per T-006's scope rule.

Related: ISS-012 (UTF-16 vs code points), ISS-015 (trim vs strip), ALLOWLIST entry 11 (the `str.isdigit()`/`int()` sliver).
title: codex.ts regexes use JS `\d` (ASCII) where Python `\d` is Unicode Nd — 3 sites, success-path totals
